title: Ranks, files and squares
objectives: Read a square's file and rank without needing to memorize notation

steps.text: Columns going up the board are called files. Rows going across are called ranks. Every square is where one file meets one rank.
Every square has a name, so players can talk about the board without pointing at it. Files are lettered a to h, left to right from White's side. This whole highlighted column is the e-file.
Ranks are numbered 1 to 8, starting from White's side of the board. This whole highlighted row is the 4th rank.
A square's name combines its file letter and its rank number. The e-file and the 4th rank meet at exactly one square: e4.

steps.prompt: Tap the e-file and 4th-rank intersection — the e4 square.

hints.text: Find the square where the e-file meets the 4th rank.
Here's the e-file and the 4th rank — find where they cross.
That square is e4 — file e, rank 4.

feedback.d4: Close, but that's d4 — one file to the left. Count again from a to e.
feedback.f4: Close, but that's f4 — one file to the right. Count again from a to e.
feedback.e3: Close, but that's e3 — one rank too low. Count again from 1 to 4.
feedback.e5: Close, but that's e5 — one rank too high. Count again from 1 to 4.
feedback.default: Not quite — count the files from the left first, then the ranks from the bottom.

steps.successExplanation: That's e4 — the e-file and the 4th rank cross exactly there.

options: A column running up the board
A row running across the board

feedback.0: That's a file, not a rank — files are the columns, lettered a to h.
feedback.2: A single square is named by combining a file and a rank, like e4 — it isn't a rank on its own.
feedback.3: Pieces (king, queen, rook, and so on) are separate from the board's own file/rank naming system.

steps.successExplanation: Right — a rank is a row running across the board, numbered 1 to 8.
